Customer to share representative prompt set and token mix by 2026-05-14

action_items: Jordan Mills: Send pricing + TCO spreadsheet by 2026-05-14

summary: Discovery focused on per-token economics and tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated and private deployments. Customer is cost-sensitive, wants predictable unit costs and gating constraints for a pilot. Key levers discussed: batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization model variants, reserved capacity and burst policies. Security/SOC2 and KMS were flagged as checklist items.
transcript:
00:00 Jordan Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Jordan from Redwood, with Priya and Alex. good to meet you all, Evan, Sofia, Caleb, and Maya. 00:10 Evan Park: Hey thanks, yeah we appreciate you making time. quick context, we're evaluating LLM infra for inference, primary use is real-time summarization and an internal insights assistant. cost is big for us. 00:25 Priya Desai: Awesome — can you give a sense of current stack and token volumes? even rough ballpark helps. 00:34 Sofia Martinez: Right now we run inference on prem for latency sensitive flows, about 6k qps at peak across services but bursty. token mix is around 70% short prompts (10-50 tokens) and 30% long sessions (2k+ tokens) for summarization. 00:50 Jordan Mills: OK that's super helpful. high-level, we typically frame the cost discussion around per-token hosted pricing, reserved GPU capacity for dedicated, and then private for air-gapped. important levers are batching, KV cache/prefix caching, quantization, and routing policies. 01:10 Caleb Reed: When you say per-token hosted pricing, is that the same as other APIs? does Redwood include hidden egress or infra fees? 01:20 Jordan Mills: Good question — hosted is per-token for input+output; no hidden egress in the bill, just usage and optional add-ons like longer observability retention. for dedicated we move to committed monthly units which gives a predictable unit cost and lower per-token effective price when amortized. 01:40 Maya Iqbal: curious about batching — how much does batching actually reduce token cost without blowing up latency for short prompt flows? 01:52 Priya Desai: So batching gives you GPU efficiency — for throughput-y workloads we can get 2-4x improvement in tokens/sec on same HW. but for tight latency SLOs we use adaptive batching and tiny buckets; also prefix/KV cache helps the most for sessions with repeated context — that lowers effective tokens we compute. 02:14 Evan Park: you said prefix cache — is that the K-V cache people talk about? would it work with our long sessions where sequence length grows? 02:23 Priya Desai: yep K-V cache, sometimes transcribed as K-V rather than KV, but it's the same. we can cache encoder states and reuse across requests which reduces compute for repeated prefixes. for long sessions the cache helps reusing the earlier tokens rather than recomputing. it does add memory footprint so part of sizing. 02:40 Sofia Martinez: memory/sizing is key — do you give guidance on GPU types and quantization knobs? our infra team is sensitive to mixed precision and potential quality regressions. 02:52 Alex Chen: we have recommended profiles per workload — e.g., Llama2-Chat quantized to 4-bit gives big cost savings but you'll want to run evals on your prompts; Redwood Optimize can run a quick sweep to suggest quant+batch configs. 03:10 Caleb Reed: If we go dedicated reserved, what's the commit model and how do burst credits work? 03:18 Jordan Mills: Dedicated is reserved pool per customer — monthly or annual commits. you can configure autoscaling policies and a burst capacity that uses on-demand capacity for short spikes. billing shows reserved vs burst usage. 03:30 Evan Park: sounds promising. what's the unit math — like cost per 1k tokens hosted vs dedicated amortized? 03:38 Jordan Mills: it's workload dependent — rough ballpark, hosted might be $0.02 to $0.08 per 1k tokens depending on model size and latency profile. dedicated amortized can drop that by 30-60% depending on utilization and commit level. we'll send a TCO with their numbers. 03:55 Maya Iqbal: those ranges are wide — do you have a simple example? say 100M tokens/month, mostly short prompts. 04:03 Priya Desai: for 100M tokens/month with batching and prefix caching applied to repeated queries, you might see an effective compute token count drop to ~70M equivalent. hosted at $0.04 per 1k tokens => approx $2.8k/mo; dedicated with a medium commit could be $1.2k-$1.8k depending on GPU choice and utilization. this is illustrative, we'll model with your token mix. 04:30 Sofia Martinez: on pricing page we saw model variants — do you support fallbacks to cheaper model variants when load spikes? 04:38 Jordan Mills: yes, routing policies can fallback to cheaper model variants or to a lower-capacity region. also can route based on customer tier or latency SLO. 04:50 Caleb Reed: from finance POV we need predictable burn. committed pricing helps, but we need to know cost per inference and worst-case. do you provide budget alerts or caps? 05:03 Alex Chen: console has token-level cost breakdowns and alerts; you can set hard caps, soft alerts, and autoscale policies to avoid surprise spend. 05:12 Evan Park: security — we need SOC2, SSO, KMS integration; private deployment might be required for some regs. what's the story there? 05:22 Jordan Mills: Redwood is SOC2 and we support SAML/SSO + RBAC. KMS integrations for dedicated and private; private deployment (VPC/on-prem) keeps data in your network and we hand over a private control plane. we'll share SOC2 and KMS docs. 05:38 Sofia Martinez: do you have customers doing on-prem because of data residency? 05:42 Priya Desai: yes, regulated customers commonly pick private. note private is higher TCO but required for compliance. 05:50 Maya Iqbal: quick nit — we've seen inference delta in quality after heavy quantization. how do you recommend validating? 05:58 Priya Desai: you run evals on a held-out prompt set — Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles and run regressions. important to evaluate both automated metrics and human pass/fail tests for generation quality. 06:15 Evan Park: timeline — we'd like a 2-week pilot, measure cost delta and latency impact, then decide to go dedicated if numbers look good. is that doable? 06:23 Jordan Mills: absolutely. typical pilot is 2 weeks: we onboard you to hosted with a dedicated project, run a cost pilot with token logging, and seed dedicated capacity if you want a baseline. 06:36 Caleb Reed: ROI to justify commit — what utilization do we need to get dedicated to be cheaper? 06:41 Alex Chen: depends on model and GPU choice but usually >40-50% sustained utilization makes a reserved pool more economical. 06:52 Sofia Martinez: for our bursty distribution maybe hybrid — reserved baseline + hosted burst — can we model that? 06:58 Jordan Mills: yes, hybrid is common — reserved capacity sized for steady-state and burst offload to hosted. we model that in the TCO sheet. 07:10 Maya Iqbal: on metrics, can you show per-route and per-model dashboards? we want to tag routes per product line. 07:17 Alex Chen: yes, console supports per-route dashboards, token-level cost attribution and tracing. 07:24 Evan Park: a little transcription note — the auto transcript sometimes garbles K-V as K-Vee, haha. 07:29 Jordan Mills: yeah Fireflies does that, we've seen it. 07:33 Sofia Martinez: any caveats on latency SLOs with batching enabled? our users expect sub-200ms p95 on short prompts. 07:40 Priya Desai: you can tune batching thresholds and use tiny-latency policy so p95 remains under target; for sub-200ms we often recommend local private or dedicated smaller batch windows and faster GPU types. 07:55 Caleb Reed: finance question — do you offer committed discounts for multi-year contracts? 08:00 Jordan Mills: yes annual commits get better rates; multi-year can be negotiated on enterprise deals. 08:08 Maya Iqbal: what's the SLA on Dedicated? 08:11 Alex Chen: we have SLA tiers; typical is 99.9% with enterprise plan, and additional on-call support for private deployments. 08:20 Evan Park: what's the onboarding time for a pilot? 08:23 Jordan Mills: onboarding can be 2-5 business days for hosted pilot; dedicated setup for small reserved pool ~1-2 weeks, private longer depending on network. 08:33 Sofia Martinez: we need to loop in security for SOC2 doc review — can you send over compliance package? 08:38 Jordan Mills: will send SOC2, penetration test summary, KMS integration guide and SSO docs. 08:45 Caleb Reed: can we get a sample invoice breakdown showing reserved vs burst usage? helps procurement. 08:50 Jordan Mills: yes, we'll include a sample bill and TCO model. 08:55 Maya Iqbal: for the pilot we'd like Redwood to run an initial optimization pass — batching and cache suggestions — to see immediate wins. 09:01 Priya Desai: absolutely, we'll run a profiling pass on sample traffic and propose batching/cache profiles as part of the pilot. 09:10 Evan Park: great. quick recaps? 09:13 Jordan Mills: recap: Jordan to send hosted vs dedicated pricing + TCO modeling; Priya will prepare performance benchmarks and optimization suggestions; customer to share token mix and prompt set; schedule SE deep-dive for 2026-05-19. 09:30 Sofia Martinez: confirmed. thanks all. 09:36 Caleb Reed: thanks. 09:40 Jordan Mills: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites. 09:45 <<call ends>>

Note: transcript has occasional mis-attributions and minor transcript artifacts, numeric times are approximate relative timestamps and not exact speaker turn timestamps.
